newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian military rescues teens from Arctic ice floe.
newsitem.headline: Canadian military rescues teens from Arctic ice floe.

text.p: A group of teenage students and their teachers were rescued by Canadian military helicopter on Thursday after being stranded on an ice floe in the Arctic for four days.
"The helicopter has picked them up. Everybody is fine," said Capt. Wayne McCrae, a spokesman for Canada's military rescue team based in Trenton, Ontario.
The 15 people were adrift off the north end of Baffin Island near Canada's border with Greenland. They became stranded on Monday during an expedition to learn traditional Eskimo ways.

The 10 students, aged 16 to 20, and five teachers were setting up camp on the ice on Monday night when high winds and strong currents broke off a chunk of the ice. The floe drifted 25 miles (40 km) from shore.
Most of the group members are Inuit, or Eskimo, from the outpost of Pond Inlet and were taking part in a trip aimed at learning traditional lifestyles and survival skills.

Because they had planned to camp on the ice until Friday, they had enough food and equipment to survive, McCrae said. They stayed in contact with authorities by radio, although their batteries ran low.
